title: 50,000+ open-source game assets in one library
author: Important-Respect-12
selftext:
hey everyone, we’re the team behind patch.

when we received our funding, there were a hundred things we could have spent it on. we kept coming back to one, supporting the open-source game dev community.

so many games start on free assets. a kenney pack, a poly haven texture, a model someone put online and asked nothing for.

**we made 5,000+ new assets ourselves** and released every one as open source.

**then we put them in one library with everyone else’s.** kenney, kaykit, poly haven, scenario and more, more than 50,000 assets in all: 3d models, materials, characters, sprites, music and sound. no more digging through ten sites and checking ten licences. every asset lists its licence and who made it.

and it’s not just single assets. there are kits too**:** procedural dungeons, skies, fire and more. pieces you can build a game with, not just props to place.

and because a lot of us build with agents now, the whole library works over **mcp and a cli**. ask your agent for a creature or a pirate ship, and it searches all 50,000 for you.

we plan to release 10000 more assets in the next 2 weeks, but this time we want to hear from game devs what specific asset pacs they struggle to find online, to prioritise accordingly. 

To access the asset library you can use pch cli, or download our app at [patch.gg](http://patch.gg) (both options completely free)

comments.author: SlRenderStudio
comments.body: where is the cli and or mcp ? why do i need to download this thing can't i browse the thing or download from the web browser ?

comments.author: Bavariasnaps
comments.body: nobody wants to be forced to registrate before he can see the models and judge if they are fitting. you can put the download button behind a wall no problem with that but we should be able to discover without a login.

replies.author: Important-Respect-12
replies.body: I agree with this and its a really valid point. We are building a web version of the toolbox, but it wasn't ready and we didn't want to postpone the release

replies.author: kirk_hsv
replies.body: You realise something isn't ready and you decide to release anyway?

replies.author: NoSloppyStakes
replies.body: The product was ready. From what it sounds like is viewing without registering wasn’t ready.

replies.author: I_pee_in_shower
replies.body: It’s not all ready. I think releasing as-is is fine with the disclosure that more is coming.

replies.author: i_rate_slop
replies.body: This is literally the key to shipping anything. Get it out there as fast as possible, then refine.

replies.author: Bavariasnaps
replies.body: ...which can also waste marketing ressources and ruin your brand reputation like with the Iphone Duo.

replies.author: i_rate_slop
replies.body:
They’re fine. 

I’ve used their PixelFx and they’re cooking. Completely changed how I approach asset design.

comments.author: phantomimp
comments.body: Why do I need to download a software? Why can't I just discover using the browser? Why do I need to be logged in to see what you have to offer?

replies.author: PerformanceComes1st
replies.body: its a free service, they need to make money somehow

replies.author: SpiralCenter
replies.body: Yeah, tell that to all the people publishing under community commons.

comments.author: lordcohliani
comments.body: Just upload them to a zip or something. Bruh moment.

comments.author: DM_me_goth_tiddies
comments.body: Should just be an API you can hit, what does the download do?

comments.author: markmandel
comments.body:
Is this actually open source? What licence is it under?

I'm looking for a repo I can look at, and not finding anything 😔

replies.author: SpiralCenter
replies.body: Does not look open source, theres no source available.

comments.author: I_pee_in_shower
comments.body:
This is a fantastic idea. What’s the catch? :)

Is access to the CLI or MCP free?

I think the best use case for this is rapid prototyping. Once you have a validating POC you can make better informed decisions about your art assets.

replies.author: I_pee_in_shower
replies.body: I’m probably gonna pass for now. I think it’s a fantastic idea and I do think you can keep your assets wherever you want but the CLI or MCP should be exposed through GitHub or a plug-in that can be reviewed before install.

comments.author: SpiralCenter
comments.body: You have to install something to use these assets?  That seems super suspicious to me.

comments.author: CodeGuyJay
comments.body:
I've been thinking about how cool it would be for someone to build a giant community asset pack. It would be awesome if there was a way to make this community driven - ie there's an mcp for others to contribute their own assets. 

Might be a great way for people to burn tokens at the end of each week - contributing to an open source asset library.. 

This seems like an awesome step in the right direction, hope you manage to pull this off!
